open.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
We're not open. Well, we are, but the bitter's not settled and I'm not serving you cloudy, so you've got ten minutes of me and a packet of crisps.
tn_publican
Reg Cheverton. You'll be the Americans. The whole town's had you for breakfast. I've heard you're from a magazine, the government, and the Mormons.
teddy
He's got three stories about us already. That's a man who sells stories, not beer.

passives.line: The photo over the bar hangs a foot left of a nail hole that's been filled and painted. It used to hang somewhere a customer could see it better.
He's got a story ready, and it's the one everybody gets. There's a second one behind it that he's saving for a better price.

options.text: None of the three. We're the ones Mrs Bannister's feeding. Crisps are fine.
Ten minutes. Then we'll want the one you don't tell the Mormons.
The Mormons. We'll take that. It gets the best seats.

crisps.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
Mrs Bannister's. Then you've had the register read at you and the Room 4 business. Right. Cheese and onion or ready salted, that's your choice in life.
tn_publican
Sit by the window. That's where the Sunnyside lot sat. Don't know why I keep saying that to people. Nobody's ever asked.

tab.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
You'll want. I've had the Sunday papers wanting, in '83, and they got the one everybody gets and a bill for the sandwiches.
miriam
He's priced us. Not the beer. Us.

hub.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
Mermaid Arms. Been Chevertons since my grandfather, and he's the one who hung that photo, so if you've a question about it you're asking a dead man through me.
hub.prompt: Reg leans on the pump and waits to be impressed.

options.text: We're from the paper. The proper one. London. We pay for pages, not pints.
That's the one everybody gets. We've already had it twice today. Tell us the other one.

fail.line: There's one story in this pub and I've told it. The other one costs more than crisps.

options.text: The hat never came off. You served him for a season. What did his hands look like?
Pint of whatever's local when it settles, and one for yourself.

static.line: The window seat. The Sunnyside seat. Something's sat in it since you came in and he's not served it. Ask him why.

paper_bluff.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
London. Right. Well, London, the pier staff reckon the camp sent a bloke down in '73 who wasn't on the books. 'The Yellow Man.' On the bill, not on the wages.
tn_publican
Ask on the pier. Ask Maureen in the Pavilion, she's got every programme since the war. Don't say it was me. Say it was a man in a pub.
teddy
He gave a London paper a name and a source in one breath. Reg has wanted to be quoted for twenty years.

bluff_fail.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
London. You've got a Sutton Office pen in your top pocket, love, and Mrs Bannister's told the butcher. Crisps are fifteen pence.
miriam
We bluffed a man whose trade is reading faces across a bar. That's on us.

second.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
...June '73. A fortnight after. A man in a grey suit came in at dinner time, sat with Alf Rudd, the boy's dad, and bought him three pints, and Alf never bought one back.
tn_publican
And after the third, Alf stood up and said it was a dog and the heat and the boy wanting his picture in the paper.
tn_publican
He'd never said it that neat before. Like he'd been given it.
tn_publican
Grey suit paid in new notes. Left a tip, which nobody did then. My dad kept the ten bob note under the till till he died. Said it felt wrong.
miriam
Somebody wrote Alf Rudd's story for him and bought him the drinks to learn it. That's not a hoax. That's a cover for one.

hands.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
...Blue. Greasepaint blue, to the wrist, under a glove he took off to drink. And he'd three fingers taped together so the hand looked wrong. Said it was part of the character.
tn_publican
Drank bitter through a straw under the brim. Never saw his face. Saw his hands every afternoon for a month.
tn_publican
I've seen them since. On the hide wall, on a kid's poster, in blue.
june
Three fingers taped. A man built a hand for the children to remember. That's not a costume. That's a signature.

hands_fail.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
I pulled pints. I didn't look at hands. You want hands, the chemist looks at hands, go and bother Harwood.
ruth
He's cross because he did look, dear. Nobody's that cross about something they didn't see.

pint.speaker: tn_publican
lines: tn_publican
...Ta. Don't tell the brewery. Right, since you're buying: the Sunnyside lot drank in the window and the one in the hat drank facing the wall. Every day. Facing the wall.
teddy
A man who faces the wall in a pub is a man who's afraid of being recognised in it.
